# the contributor audit: canonical source reduction and stratified rate centers

Read `candidate c106b596b70bfd05`, including the new Section 4a, and `candidate 237f4727836ebab9`, Sections 1--6. Read the direct prelimit affine-slice note in full. PASS with the qualifications below. These are structural and auxiliary center theorems, not OC.

## 1. Same sampled parameter, at most k(P) planes

The positive source-base hull is a lattice polytope. Its inclusion-maximal faces containing relative-interior lattice points cover every positive source, and chosen relative-interior witnesses have disjoint occupied parities by the face-join midpoint argument. Hence there are at most k(P) faces.

Each witness is a strict positive combination of all positive sources on its face. Actual deepest interpolation and L equality therefore force any sampled touching majorant at that witness to touch all those sources. The minimum V of these planes is positive and concave on the canonical hull, majorizes L on sampled fibers, and agrees at every original positive source. Testing the original radial-cone certificate with V gives integral(V-L)dnu=0. Since nu has positive density on each full sampled fiber and the gap is continuous, V=L on every sampled fiber, including boundaries.

The old unsampled extension need not be dominated by those planes. The proof correctly uses its convex sublevel {A<=L}, and uses a convex equality contact cell only for the new global minimum V. The retained row barycenters and L moments give V-Jensen equality row by row. This certifies every new radial direction h+cV concave, without claiming T_V is contained in T_L.

For a specified joint separator, the same pure-body coefficients and its original cap/contact allocations remain usable under the response formulas and joint-cone decomposition explicitly stated in Section 4a. No arbitrary parameter certificate is promoted to a physical one. The optional quadratic contraction changes the parameter certificate and must remain separate; its finite compactness and all-cone preservation are otherwise valid. Global attainment, when needed for the new representative's global minimizing property, remains part of the application framework.

The reduction preserves source weights and all sampled inverse/rate laws. Its finite plane count does not itself allocate a surface or inverse-defect budget among cells, and applying a mixed center theorem independently to each largest cell could lose an additional parity factor.

## 2. Exact strata and direct center bounds

Cross-fiber measure domination forces equal affine support dimension and tangent for every input to an integer-output relation. Therefore distinct (q,V) strata have disjoint original parity sets and are individually lattice-complete. Their sampled support hulls have exactly the original support fibers; no additional integer fiber is introduced.

The weighted atomic midpoint theorem uses actual geometric midpoints in the full embedding and arbitrary positive weights. Its finite threshold proof handles closed boundaries correctly. The intrinsic-support Helly argument also checks: ordinary Helly chooses at most q+1 constraints in each fixed fiber, projection gives convex sets on the finite base, and occupied-parity Helly chooses at most k such projected sets. The resulting relative Helly number is at most (q+1)k. Compactness of the support and closed high-mass convex sets gives a deterministic center for an arbitrary finite Borel measure, including atoms.

Choosing the largest stratum mass-to-cost ratio then gives the unnormalized mass bound W/sum_c((q_c+1)k_c). For q<=1 this is at least W/(2k), which is at least Gamma_N W/k. In normalized depth notation all these displayed mass bounds must be divided by W. This settles only the stated existential rate-measure center problem.

## 3. Hollow projections and the preserved numerical parameter

The perpendicular graph belongs to the anchored representation space. The existing canonical integer graph lift makes it affine while preserving every integer-output relation and exactly the occupied parity count. The residual-density ball-fiber construction consequently gives one whole-stratum uniform convex lift, without overlapping maximal-face covers.

Its integer rank can increase. The transfer therefore requires a previously established Gamma_N/k occupied-parity theorem, not merely Gamma_N/2^rank. The source explicitly retains this stronger numerical inductive input rather than asserting it. No general theorem at dimension N is proved by this lift alone.

## 4. Direct actual slices

Solving a nonzero continuous affine coefficient by an isometric chart preserves integer bases and exact H_(d-1) in every fiber. Positive coarea mass supplies one full continuous fiber; together with the affine span of all nonempty sampled bases, its canonical hull has the claimed full relative dimension. Boundary fibers remain present, saturated lattice coordinates are legitimate, and constant restrictions of halfspace functionals give the whole support when containing the selected point. The d=1 counting and zero-dimensional singleton cases are covered separately.

Induction applied BEFORE taking the limit thus supplies actual slice centers if the lower-dimensional theorem is available. It does not identify their incidence with the original selected cap law. Abstract limiting closed caps can carry more mass than retained moving-cap selections, as the exact global critical-cover example demonstrates. These are distinct issues from lattice preservation or the validity of the auxiliary center theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
